blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The most durable client relationships are the ones in which, over time, the boundary between supplier and partner becomes slightly indistinct. Both sides know who pays for what, of course; but both also quietly contribute to the other's success in ways that do not appear on any invoice. Those relationships survive recessions, leadership changes and price pressure that would have ended lesser arrangements many years earlier.

What creates them is not, in the end, any particular negotiation technique. It is a decade or more of small, consistent moments in which each side chose to behave slightly better than strictly required — the invoice flagged before the client noticed the error, the quiet warning about a risk not yet seen, the willingness to push back honestly when the client was about to make a mistake. These are the deposits that, over years, compound into a relationship that is almost impossible for a competitor to dislodge.

At Czarnikow's scale and tradition, the discipline is organisational rather than personal. Partnerships of this kind require not only individual account managers who believe in them, but systems of memory, handover and institutional continuity that allow the relationship to survive the inevitable rotation of the people involved. That is much harder than it sounds, and it is part of what Czarnikow's longevity has been built on.

items.q: According to the text, what happens to the boundary between supplier and partner in the most durable relationships?
options: It is formally redefined in the contract
It is enforced more strictly each year
It becomes slightly indistinct over time
It disappears entirely from the first day
items.why: "the boundary between supplier and partner becomes slightly indistinct" — ela se dilui, mas não some por contrato.

items.q: What does the author say actually creates these relationships?
options: Small, consistent moments of behaving better than required
items.why: "a decade or more of small, consistent moments in which each side chose to behave slightly better than strictly required".

items.q: Why does the text say the discipline at Czarnikow is organisational rather than personal?
options: Because clients prefer dealing with systems, not people
Because the relationship must survive the rotation of the people involved
Because individual managers are not trusted
items.why: "systems of memory, handover and institutional continuity that allow the relationship to survive the inevitable rotation of the people involved".

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A brilliant negotiation tactic is what secures a decade-long partnership
Frequent staff rotation is a genuine threat to long relationships
Generosity that never appears on an invoice can strengthen a relationship
Small consistent gestures compound over time
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente que não é uma técnica de negociação que cria essas relações.

items.q: The phrase "deposits that... compound" suggests that the author sees the relationship as…
options: Something that grows in value as small acts accumulate
A cost that must be minimised
A liability the supplier carries alone
A one-off transaction settled at signing
items.why: Inferência: a metáfora financeira (depósitos que rendem juros compostos) indica valor que cresce com o acúmulo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver preparando a transferência de uma conta de trinta anos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, this is the account I've carried for the best part of thirty years, and I want to be honest with you: most of what matters here isn't in the file. The contract you can read in an afternoon. The relationship took decades.

Let me give you one example. Every spring, before their audit, I send Margaret a note flagging anything on our side that looks messy — even small things, even things they'd probably never catch. It costs me an hour. It's bought us twenty years of trust. Do that. Don't wait for them to ask.

The harder part is knowing when to push back. There have been three or four moments where they were about to make a genuine mistake, and my job was to say so — politely, but plainly. They didn't always thank me at the time. They remembered afterwards. A supplier says yes; a partner tells you the truth.

My worry, honestly, is continuity. This can't live in your head the way it's lived in mine. Write the small things down, hand them on, and build the memory into the system — because one day you'll be doing exactly this handover, and the relationship has to outlast both of us.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Oliver, where does most of what matters about the account live?
options: Not in the file — in the relationship built over decades
items.why: "most of what matters here isn't in the file... The relationship took decades."

items.q: What does Oliver do every spring before the client's audit?
options: Sends Margaret a note flagging anything messy on his own side
Waits for the client to raise any issues
Requests an extension on the deadline
items.why: "I send Margaret a note flagging anything on our side that looks messy... Don't wait for them to ask."

items.q: How did the client react when Oliver pushed back and told them they were about to make a mistake?
options: They didn't always thank him at the time, but remembered afterwards
They thanked him immediately every time
items.why: "They didn't always thank me at the time. They remembered afterwards."

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "A supplier says yes; a partner tells you the truth"?
options: Suppliers are more reliable than partners
Partners should never disagree with clients
Clients dislike being told the truth
Honest disagreement is what distinguishes a partner from a mere vendor
items.why: Inferência: discordar com honestidade é o que eleva a relação de fornecedor a parceiro.

items.q: What is Oliver's main concern about the handover?
options: That the price will need to be renegotiated
That the knowledge lives in his head and must be built into the system to last
That his colleague is not experienced enough
That the client will leave once he retires
items.why: Inferência: "This can't live in your head... build the memory into the system... the relationship has to outlast both of us."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "No competitor has managed to dislodge us from that account in twenty years." To dislodge means to…
options: force out of an established position
items.why: Dislodge = deslocar/remover de uma posição consolidada.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Flagging the error before the client noticed was a small ___ that paid off years later."
items.why: Relational deposit = depósito relacional: um gesto que rende confiança ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "The firm's institutional continuity meant the relationship survived three changes of leadership." This refers to…
options: the length of a single manager's career
the size of the client's budget
the organisation's ability to sustain knowledge and relationships across staff changes
items.why: Continuidade institucional = a capacidade da organização de manter conhecimento e relações apesar da rotatividade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "What separates a vendor from a partner is a kind of ___ that never shows up on the invoice."
items.why: Quiet generosity = generosidade discreta: o gesto que não é cobrado, mas fideliza.

items.q: "It is a genuinely long-dated relationship — thirty years and counting." A long-dated relationship is one that…
options: extends over a very long horizon
items.why: Long-dated = de longo prazo, com horizonte muito extenso (termo tomado do jargão financeiro).

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem na gestão de contas de longo prazo. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Part of my job was to push back on the client when they were about to make a mistake." To push back on means to…
items.why: Push back on = discordar/resistir de forma respeitosa, sem simplesmente rejeitar.

items.q: "We agreed the plan, but nobody followed through on the small commitments." They…
options: failed to carry the commitments to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "I need to hand over the account before I retire." To hand over means to…
items.why: Hand over = transferir a responsabilidade/gestão da conta a outra pessoa.

items.q: "None of the paperwork will move the needle — it's the trust that keeps them with us." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, negado, significa que não muda nada relevante.

items.q: "Over thirty years, those small gestures really added up." To add up here means to…
items.why: Add up = somar-se ao longo do tempo até virar algo significativo (efeito cumulativo).
